question.problem:
The lifetime of bulbs produced by a company is normally distributed with a mean of $5\,500$ hours, and a standard deviation of $1\,100$ hours. What is the probability that a randomly selected bulb lasts more than $7\,000$ hours? Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.06\,$ | $\,0.07\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.2\,$ | $\,0.8944\,$ | $\,0.8962\,$ | $\,0.8980\,$ |
| $\,1.3\,$ | $\,0.9115\,$ | $\,0.9131\,$ | $\,0.9147\,$ |
| $\,1.4\,$ | $\,0.9265\,$ | $\,0.9279\,$ | $\,0.9292\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the lifetime of the selected bulb. Then we have $X∼N(5\,500,1\,{100}^{2}).$

We want to find $P(X>7\,000).$ Thus, we convert $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>7\,000) & =P(Z>\frac{7\,000-5\,500}{1\,100}) \\  & =P(Z>1.36) \\  & =1-P(Z\le 1.36) \\  & =1-Φ(1.36)\end{aligned}
$$

From the $z$-table, we see that

$$
1-Φ(1.36)=1-0.9131=0.0869.
$$

Therefore, the probability that a randomly selected bulb lasts more than $7\,000$ hours is approximately $0.09.$
